:::: {.tk-cols}
::: {.tk-col}
Designing, controlling and assessing a fusion reactor means running plasma simulations
thousands of times. The physics codes that are accurate enough take hours per run. Neural
networks trained on those codes run in milliseconds, but a network returns an answer
for any input, including inputs far outside its training data.

**The Tokamak Toolkit** is an integrated tokamak simulation in which any expensive physics module can be
swapped for a neural surrogate, but only behind a *guard*. At every radius and every time step
the surrogate has to show that it is inside the conditions it was trained on, that its
ensemble agrees with itself, and that its answer is physically possible. Where it can't, a
trusted physics model takes over, and the handover is recorded. The whole simulation is
written in JAX, so it compiles to one program and can be differentiated end to end, and it
speaks IMAS, the fusion community's standard data format, at every boundary.

The code is private for now. What is public is the argument: the method, the checks that
define "correct", every number with where it came from, and the mistakes.
[How this is built](about.qmd): the code is written by AI coding agents, Claude and Codex,
working to a brief by a human owner who makes every physics, licence and publication decision.
:::

```{=html}
<svg class="tk-diagram tk-physics" viewBox="0 0 1200 960" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-labelledby="tkp-title tkp-desc">
<title id="tkp-title">How the physics codes in the Tokamak Toolkit exchange information</title>
<desc id="tkp-desc">Diagram. TORAX, the core transport solver, sits in the centre and evolves electron and ion temperature, electron density and poloidal flux. Above it, the equilibrium: a prescribed CHEASE EQDSK for the ITER hybrid scenario supplies flux-surface geometry every step; FreeGSNKE computes MAST-U-like free-boundary equilibria from coil currents and its two-way coupling to TORAX is planned. On the left, the sources: TORAX sends density, temperature and Z_eff; RF heating (Gaussian deposition), ASCOT5 fusion alphas (with the magnetic field from the EQDSK, updated outside the loop and held between updates) and other TORAX source models return heat, particle and current sources. On the right, the transport coefficients: TORAX sends gradients, q, magnetic shear, temperature ratio and collisionality; QLKNN, a neural network trained offline on QuaLiKiz, and the Bohm/gyro-Bohm fallback both feed the guard, which picks one per face; with the Sauter neoclassical model they return diffusivities, convection, bootstrap current and conductivity. Below, the pedestal and sawtooth models exchange pressure and q for edge values and profile resets, and TORAX writes profiles, sources and fluxes to IMAS IDSs. A separate offline branch takes the CHEASE EQDSK or a saved TORAX state through a unit and input adapter into JOREK. Its run wrapper records provenance for fixed-boundary equilibria and linear pedestal-stability scans. Native HDF5 energies and perturbations provide growth rates and mode locations. ITER hybrid time-step checks have passed; grid convergence is open. There is no JOREK feedback into TORAX or trained JOREK surrogate.</desc>

<figcaption>How the physics codes exchange information during a run. TORAX solves core
transport; the other codes supply its geometry, transport coefficients and sources. The JOREK
branch analyses MHD stability offline from the EQDSK or a saved TORAX state, with no feedback
into the transport loop. Its ITER hybrid time-step checks have passed; grid convergence is
still open. Hover over a box for what it does.
<a href="technical/jorek.qmd">JOREK implementation and checks</a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
```
:::

:::: {.tk-notes}
::: {.tk-note data-node="core"}
**Core transport: TORAX.** The open-source JAX transport code. On a radial grid in ρ it evolves
the electron and ion temperatures, the electron density and the poloidal flux ψ (current
diffusion), with an implicit solve every time step (Newton-Raphson, with Picard iteration as a
fallback). The Tokamak Toolkit calls TORAX's own single-step function from a fixed-step compiled loop, so a
whole run is one program that can be differentiated end to end. Entries 1 to 3.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="eqdsk"}
**Prescribed equilibrium.** The CHEASE equilibrium of the ITER hybrid scenario, shipped with
TORAX as an EQDSK file. TORAX builds its flux-surface geometry (volumes, areas, metric
coefficients) from it. ASCOT5 takes its magnetic field from the same file, with the poloidal
flux scaled to TORAX's plasma current. JOREK uses the same separatrix boundary for its
ITER stability reference cases: the EQDSK profiles in case (a), and profiles derived from
a saved TORAX state in case (b).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="fgs"}
**Free-boundary equilibrium: FreeGSNKE.** Solves the free-boundary Grad-Shafranov equation for
the MAST-U-like machine description and writes an IMAS equilibrium IDS. Not yet coupled to
transport: that needs a turbulence model valid on a spherical tokamak, which QLKNN is not.
Entry 6.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="coils"}
**Coil currents.** The poloidal-field coil currents, with the coil, passive-structure and wall
geometry of the machine description, are the input to the free-boundary solve.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="ascot"}
**Fusion alphas: ASCOT5.** AFSI computes where D-T fusion alphas are born from TORAX's density
and temperature profiles. ASCOT5 follows each alpha along its guiding-centre orbit while it slows
down on electrons and ions, or is lost. The power given to electrons and to ions is mapped back
to TORAX's grid and replaces TORAX's local alpha-heating model. ASCOT5 runs outside the compiled
loop; its result is held as a prescribed source until the next update. Entries 10, 12 and 15.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rf"}
**RF heating.** A radial Gaussian deposition of RF power to electrons, normalised to the
requested absorbed power, with an optional co-located driven current. This is the physics model an RF
deposition surrogate would fall back to. Entry 5.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="src"}
**Other sources.** TORAX's own source models: auxiliary heating, ohmic heating, radiation,
electron-ion heat exchange, gas puff and pellet fuelling. Which ones are active depends on the
scenario configuration.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="qlk"}
**QuaLiKiz.** A quasilinear gyrokinetic turbulence code. QLKNN was trained on its output,
offline; the Tokamak Toolkit does not run QuaLiKiz itself.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="qlknn"}
**QLKNN.** A neural network that returns turbulent heat and particle fluxes from local plasma
parameters (normalised gradients, q, magnetic shear, temperature ratio, collisionality) in
microseconds. Entry 4.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="bgb"}
**Bohm/gyro-Bohm.** An empirical transport model. It is used at each face where the guard
rejects the surrogate ([OQ-1](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-1)).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="guard"}
**The guard.** At every radial face and every time step, the surrogate's output is kept only if
its inputs are inside the training domain and its outputs are finite and within bounds.
Otherwise the fallback value is used and the substitution is recorded. Entry 4.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="neo"}
**Neoclassical.** TORAX's Sauter model: the bootstrap current and the plasma conductivity used
in current diffusion.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="mhd"}
**Pedestal and sawteeth.** TORAX's pedestal model sets the temperature and density at the
pedestal top, the outer boundary of the core solve. Its sawtooth model flattens the core
profiles inside the q = 1 surface when the trigger condition is met.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="imas"}
**IMAS IDSs.** The Tokamak Toolkit writes its state as IMAS data structures (core_profiles, core_sources,
core_transport, equilibrium). Unit and coordinate conversions happen only in these adapters.
FreeGSNKE writes its own equilibrium IDS.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="jorek-inputs"}
**JOREK stability inputs.** Case (a) takes the CHEASE EQDSK pressure and FF′. Case (b) uses
pressure and current from the saved TORAX ITER hybrid state, on the same EQDSK separatrix.
JOREK solves a new equilibrium: case (b) scales FF′ to match the target plasma current,
so its safety-factor profile differs from TORAX's fixed-geometry state. This is an offline
snapshot, not a time-step coupling. [Input cases](technical/jorek.qmd#case-b-equilibrium).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="jorek-adapter"}
**JOREK input adapter.** Converts SI/eV to JOREK's normalised units and writes profile files
and namelists on the host, outside JAX. Physics choices are explicit inputs. Output is read
from native HDF5 restart files, rather than an IMAS IDS.
[Adapter](technical/jorek.qmd#adapter).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="jorek"}
**JOREK and run wrapper.** An external Tier A MHD reference. The implemented ITER workflow
solves fixed-boundary equilibria and scans toroidal mode number for linear pedestal stability.
The wrapper snapshots inputs and the executable, launches MPI/OpenMP runs, classifies
failures and timeouts, and retains outputs with provenance. It is never called inside the
compiled transport loop. [Run wrapper](technical/jorek.qmd#runner).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="jorek-analysis"}
**Stability analysis.** Fits growth rates from magnetic and kinetic energies, locates the
perturbations, and compares time-step and grid checks. The ITER hybrid pedestal modes have
passed the time-step check; grid convergence remains open, so the growth rates are not yet
accepted under the full convergence criterion. There is no feedback into TORAX and no trained
JOREK surrogate; the later role remains a decision for the owner.
[Checks and limits](technical/jorek.qmd#ceilings).
:::
::::

<!-- Run-tracking section hidden for now (owner, 2 Oct 2026). Quarto drops .content-hidden
     from the rendered page; delete the wrapper to show it again. -->
::::: {.content-hidden}
## How each run is recorded

Every command that runs physics keeps a run record ([entry 9](log/09-run-tracking.qmd)). The
record is written on the host after the compiled loop returns, so tracking cannot change a
result. A local copy is always written; [Simvue](https://simvue.io) receives a mirror of it.

::: {.tk-flow}
```{=html}
<figure class="tk-physics-fig">
<!-- SVG below is written by blog/figures/make_run_tracking.py; edit the script, not the SVG -->
<!-- tracking-svg:start -->
<svg class="tk-diagram tk-tracking" viewBox="0 0 1200 610" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-labelledby="tkr-title tkr-desc">
<title id="tkr-title">How each Tokamak Toolkit run is recorded and mirrored to Simvue</title>
<desc id="tkr-desc">Diagram. On the left, the Tokamak Toolkit commands that run physics: torax, torax-loop, benchmark-raptor, equilibrium, ascot-alpha, ascot-apply and run, plus dataset generation (M2) and surrogate training (M3). Each opens one run record. In the middle, the life of a run: start_run records the configuration and provenance (git commit, package versions, configuration hash, input hashes); log_params records the settings; the compiled loop runs with no tracking calls inside and returns its full trace; log_series then writes one record per step with the step number and simulation time; alerts and events are raised; output files are saved with their provenance; finish marks the run completed or failed. On the right, every call goes to two places: a local record under runs/, always written, and a Simvue mirror. On a login node the mirror writes to the Simvue server directly; inside a SLURM job it writes to an offline cache, which make simvue-push uploads from a login node. On the server each run sits in folder /tkit/&lt;command&gt; with tags, metadata, metrics against step and simulation time, events, alerts and files. If Simvue cannot start, the run continues on the local record.</desc>
```

:::

:::: {.tk-notes}
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-torax"}
**torax.** Runs a TORAX scenario with TORAX's own driver (adaptive time step). Records the
scenario, tolerance and TORAX version, the TORAX output series per output time, the wall time,
and the output file with its provenance. Alert if TORAX does not complete.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-loop"}
**torax-loop.** The Tokamak Toolkit's fixed-step loop over TORAX. Per step: axis T~e~, T~i~ and n~e~,
thermal energy, solver error flag, inner iterations, sawtooth crashes, and the fraction of faces
where the guard used the fallback. Alert if the solver stalls.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-bench"}
**benchmark-raptor.** The ITER L-mode benchmark against RAPTOR. Records the deviation of each
profile and trace from both published curves. Alerts if a quantity is outside the tolerance set
at the physicist review, if the loop and TORAX's driver disagree, or if the solver stalls.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-eq"}
**equilibrium.** A FreeGSNKE free-boundary solve. Records every coil current, the plasma
current and its error against the target, the magnetic-axis position, the wall time and the
IMAS equilibrium file.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-alpha"}
**ascot-alpha.** The ASCOT5 alpha-particle run, submitted to the cluster. Records the inputs,
the AFSI birth rate against TORAX's, the power deposited on electrons and ions, and the end
conditions of the markers. Alerts if the birth rates disagree or too much power is unfinished.
Inside a SLURM job the Simvue mirror writes offline.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-apply"}
**ascot-apply.** Restarts TORAX with the ASCOT5 alpha heating as a prescribed source and
compares it with TORAX's local model. Records both heating profiles' totals, the restart series
and the restart files.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-toy"}
**run.** The toy Tier A models from M0. Records the per-step trace and benchmark errors; alert
on a Picard stall or a benchmark failure.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-data"}
**Dataset generation (M2).** `tglf-dataset`: one run per dataset, tagged by machine and
version, with per-chunk metrics; the finished file and its provenance are saved to the run, so
a training run can identify its data by hash. Entry 17.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-train"}
**Surrogate training (M3).** Opens its run through the tracking interface, with dataset hashes
and model configuration in its provenance. Records training and validation losses per epoch,
held-out scores, and the final checkpoint with its metadata and provenance.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-start"}
**start_run.** Opens the record. Provenance: time, package version, git commit and whether the
working tree had uncommitted changes (read when the process starts), Python, JAX and platform,
tier, the producing command, the full configuration and its hash, and the hashes of input files.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-params"}
**log_params.** The settings of this run, e.g. scenario, time step, number of steps, tolerance,
device, code versions.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-jit"}
**Compiled loop.** The whole time loop is one compiled JAX program. It makes no tracking calls,
writes no files, and returns one row per step.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-series"}
**log_series.** After the loop returns, one metric record per step, stamped with the step number
and the simulation time in seconds. Simvue rejects non-finite values; the local record keeps
them and an alert is raised once per metric.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-alert"}
**Alerts and events.** Named alerts (e.g. solver_stall, acceptance, afsi_mismatch,
non_finite_metric) are logged as events and set to critical in Simvue, optionally with an email.
An exception inside the run is logged as an event before the run is marked failed.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-artifact"}
**log_artifact.** Copies each output file into the record with its provenance JSON. In Simvue
the configuration and provenance are saved as inputs, the results as outputs.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-finish"}
**finish.** Status completed, or failed if an exception left the run. The Simvue queue is
flushed before a failed status is set, so no records are lost.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-local"}
**Local record.** A directory per run under runs/, named by start time and command. It is
written first and is complete even when Simvue is unavailable.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-online"}
**Online.** On a login node the mirror sends each call to the server as it happens.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-offline"}
**Offline.** Cluster compute nodes have no internet access, so inside a SLURM job the mirror
writes to a cache on the work file system.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-push"}
**make simvue-push.** Uploads the offline cache from a login node with Simvue's sender. Safe to
repeat: a run uploaded in several goes becomes one server run.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rt-server"}
**Simvue server.** Each run has the same name as its local record, sits in folder
/tkit/‹command› (/tkit-validation for test runs) and carries the tags tkit, tier-A or tier-B,
and the command. Its metadata holds the flattened configuration, provenance and SLURM job ids,
so runs can be filtered and compared in the runs table.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
/* Hover descriptions for the diagrams: each SVG box carries data-node="<id>", matched to a
   .tk-note[data-node] block in a hidden .tk-notes container above. */
(function () {
  var tip = null;
  function show(html, x, y) {
    tip.innerHTML = html;
    tip.style.display = "block";
    var w = tip.offsetWidth, h = tip.offsetHeight;
    var left = Math.min(x + 14, window.innerWidth - w - 8);
    var top = y + 16 + h > window.innerHeight ? y - h - 12 : y + 16;
    tip.style.left = Math.max(8, left) + "px";
    tip.style.top = Math.max(8, top) + "px";
  }
  function hide() { if (tip) tip.style.display = "none"; }
  window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    var notes = {};
    document.querySelectorAll(".tk-notes .tk-note").forEach(function (n) {
      notes[n.dataset.node] = n.innerHTML;
    });
    tip = document.createElement("div");
    tip.className = "tk-tip";
    tip.setAttribute("role", "tooltip");
    document.body.appendChild(tip);
    document.querySelectorAll(".tk-flow svg g[data-node]").forEach(function (g) {
      var html = notes[g.dataset.node];
      if (!html) return;
      g.classList.add("tk-has-note");
      g.addEventListener("mousemove", function (e) { show(html, e.clientX, e.clientY); });
      g.addEventListener("mouseleave", hide);
      g.addEventListener("click", function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); show(html, e.clientX, e.clientY); });
    });
    document.addEventListener("click", hide);
    window.addEventListener("scroll", hide, { passive: true });
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Milestones

Each milestone has acceptance criteria fixed in advance; three of them end in a review by a
human expert, not by the agent that built the code.

| | milestone | what it delivers | state | human gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | [Scaffold](milestones/M0.qmd) | data structures, the guard, the coupling loop, IMAS adapters, tests | [done 18 Sep 2026]{.wf .done} | — |
| M1 | [Open baseline](milestones/M1.qmd) | open-source physics codes wired in; a published benchmark reproduced | [done 1 Oct 2026]{.wf .done} | [physicist review: passed]{.wf .done} |
| M2 | [Training data](milestones/M2.qmd) | sampled datasets from first-principles turbulence codes, with provenance | [done 3 Oct 2026]{.wf .done} | — |
| M3 | [Surrogates](milestones/M3.qmd) | neural ensembles with physics built in, running inside the loop | [done 10 Oct 2026]{.wf .done} | — |
| M4 | [Verification](milestones/M4.qmd) | evidence package and guarded model records | [transport bounds unresolved]{.wf .crit} | [certification pending]{.wf .todo} |
| M5 | [Uncertainty and validation](milestones/M5.qmd) | ITER prior propagation, sensitivity and reference-label calibration | [temporal convergence unresolved]{.wf .crit} | [physicist sign-off pending]{.wf .todo} |

## What's next

The [action plan](action-plan.qmd) gives dependencies and completion criteria.

- **M4: verification.** The bounded transport investigation closes scientifically unresolved ([both full-box pilots retain nonfinite physical enclosures after all final objectives run; independent graph, constraint and corrected-dual replay passes, with no finite physical candidate]{.claim}[C-297](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-297){.cid .st-preliminary}). The four records, guard integration and cheap CI re-proof retain the EC-robustness and MAST-U limitations. Exact proof boxes remain separate from ordinary guard margins ([all four verified input boxes match the previous loaders; 48 of 48 retained pedestal states keep identical predictions and decisions; none of the 57 EC states is inside the exact proof boxes, so no EC certificate-based output check applies there]{.claim}[C-284](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-284){.cid .st-measured}). The revised report-only fallback alert policy is adopted under [OQ-50](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-50); certification remains pending.
- **JOREK stability (alongside M4).** The time-step checks pass, but the doubled-grid checks remain incomplete and the existing resource projection rule stops further links ([all three selected fine-grid checks remain incomplete; the measured-cost projection exceeds the existing compute envelope and further submissions stop]{.claim}[C-291](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-291){.cid .st-preliminary}). No fine-grid growth rate or stability verdict follows.
- **M5: uncertainty and validation.** The historical prior study remains available ([all 256 retained Monte Carlo outputs are finite with zero native linear-step error codes, and 2048 sensitivity evaluations drop no rows; those codes do not establish nonlinear-residual or temporal convergence]{.claim}[C-292](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-292){.cid .st-measured}), with nonlinear flags ([all four outputs fail the fixed 10% standard-deviation cross-check; disagreements are 46.2%, 43.4%, 43.1% and 59.7% for fusion power, thermal energy, central electron temperature and central ion temperature]{.claim}[C-287](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-287){.cid .st-measured}). Finer ladders still fail temporal convergence ([maximum paired changes remain 19.2654% and 1.9773% across the two refinements, exceeding the fixed 1% limit; all 99 retained rows are finite with zero native linear-step error codes and no exclusions]{.claim}[C-295](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-295){.cid .st-preliminary}, [the additional finer ladder has maximum paired changes of 1.7092% and 1.8560%, above the unchanged 1% criterion; all 99 assessed rows remain valid and no supported replacement step is established]{.claim}[C-296](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-296){.cid .st-preliminary}); the next ladder passes one pair but fails the finer pair ([the first pair stays below 1%, but the finer pair changes fusion power by up to 4.1372% and fails three quantities; all 99 assessed rows remain valid, so no replacement step is supported]{.claim}[C-298](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-298){.cid .st-preliminary}). The completed internal diagnostic establishes branch mismatch and a local residual contribution ([the failing case has different last-guess and accepted-state branches on 39.453% of coarse and 73.145% of fine steps over (3,5] seconds; during (3.5,4.5] seconds all fine accepted states fall back while 84.961% of last guesses select the surrogate]{.claim}[C-300](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-300){.cid .st-measured}, [the fine failing case has branch-term norm ratios of 0.723 for electron temperature and 0.982 for ion temperature; the signed global branch term cancels and the remaining coefficient lag carries the net defect]{.claim}[C-301](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-301){.cid .st-measured}); a checkpoint probe remains prepared only. Final uncertainty requires a supported step and an affordable complete design. Physicist review still needs the stated priors and unquantified pedestal/equilibrium discrepancy ([K-035](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-035)).
- **Profile Newton separately** ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)), distinguishing compilation, ensemble evaluation and
  Jacobian cost. Historical speed-up belongs to v1.
- **ASCOT5 follow-ups, before neutral-beam ions**: the alphas' mean birth energy ([K-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-011)) and the
  core heating profile ([K-012](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-012)).
- **Future extension:** extending the benchmark to a STEP power-plant flat-top is planned as a
  future extension. For now the work stays with the ITER benchmark and MAST-U.
